summary.title: Enabling Real-Time Conversations with Minimal Training Costs
summary.authors: Wang Xu, Shuo Wang, Weilin Zhao, Xu Han, Yukun Yan, Yudi Zhang, Zhe Tao, Zhiyuan Liu, Wanxiang Che
summary.field_subfield: Natural Language Processing / Large Language Models
summary.executive_summary: This paper introduces DUO (DUplex decOding), a novel channel-division-multiplexing strategy designed to equip Large Language Models (LLMs) with duplex capabilities—specifically the ability to listen and speak simultaneously—without the substantial computational retraining costs associated with existing time-division methods. While prior duplex models like MiniCPM-Duplex require splitting and mixing input/output in time slices, necessitating massive datasets (~5,000K samples) and extensive training (36 hours on 40 GPUs), DUO operates by running parallel decoding branches. It uses state tokens (<1> for queries, <2> for non-queries) to manage channel transitions, allowing the model to process user interruptions or silence while continuing to generate responses. The authors trained a MiniCPM-2.4B model on only 10K samples for 25 minutes on 8 GPUs. Human evaluations and standard benchmarks demonstrate that DUO achieves superior responsiveness and human-likeness compared to the baseline MiniCPM-Duplex while maintaining comparable factuality and faithfulness. Crucially, DUO preserves the original model's capabilities on standard benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, etc.) better than the time-division baseline, which suffers performance drops when trained on smaller datasets. The method effectively handles both interruption and non-awakening interactions, offering a resource-efficient path toward real-time conversational AI.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper introduces DUO (DUplex decOding), a novel channel-division-multiplexing strategy designed to equip Large Language Models (LLMs) with duplex capabilities—specifically the ability to listen and speak simultaneously—without the substantial computational retraining costs associated with existing time-division methods. While prior duplex models like MiniCPM-Duplex require splitting and mixing input/output in time slices, necessitating massive datasets (~5,000K samples) and extensive training (36 hours on 40 GPUs), DUO operates by running parallel decoding branches. It uses state tokens (<1> for queries, <2> for non-queries) to manage channel transitions, allowing the model to process user interruptions or silence while continuing to generate responses. The authors trained a MiniCPM-2.4B model on only 10K samples for 25 minutes on 8 GPUs. Human evaluations and standard benchmarks demonstrate that DUO achieves superior responsiveness and human-likeness compared to the baseline MiniCPM-Duplex while maintaining comparable factuality and faithfulness. Crucially, DUO preserves the original model's capabilities on standard benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, etc.) better than the time-division baseline, which suffers performance drops when trained on smaller datasets. The method effectively handles both interruption and non-awakening interactions, offering a resource-efficient path toward real-time conversational AI.

Research Context
Conventional LLM dialogue systems operate on a turn-based paradigm. This turn-based nature precludes real-time interaction during response generation. Researchers have proposed duplex models to facilitate real-time interactive feedback. However, these duplex methods typically require substantial computational resources. Existing approaches often diverge substantially from the backbone model. Prior methods like MiniCPM-Duplex employ a time-division-multiplexing strategy. These time-division methods split and mix input and output in a time slice format. Such structural changes demand significant computing power for model retraining.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can LLMs be equipped with duplex capabilities using minimal additional training? Does a channel-based parallel decoding approach outperform time-division methods? The authors hypothesize that DUO enhances naturalness with minimal training costs. It is predicted that DUO will support simultaneous listening and thinking. The method aims to address the limitation of passive waiting in current systems. Hypothesis: DUO will maintain original model capabilities better than retrained baselines. The study tests if DUO improves responsiveness and human-likeness. The authors predict that DUO handles non-awakening interactions effectively.

Methodological Details
The study utilizes MiniCPM-2.4B as the foundation model. A dataset of 10K samples was constructed for training. This dataset size is significantly smaller than the 5,000K used by MiniCPM-Duplex. Training was conducted on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs. The training process took approximately 25 minutes. The learning rate was set to 1e-5 with a constant scheduler. The batch size used during training was 112. The maximum sequence length was set to 4,096. Two state tokens were introduced: <1> for queries and <2> for non-queries. The input channel predicted tokens alpha were set to 4. Human evaluation involved 40 multi-turn dialogue sessions per model. Three participants with Bachelor's degrees conducted the human evaluation. Evaluation criteria included responsiveness, human-likeness, faithfulness, and factuality. Standard benchmarks were evaluated using the UltraEval platform. Benchmarks included CMMLU, MMLU, BBH, HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, and ARC.

Procedures And Architectures
DUO employs a channel-division-multiplexing decoding strategy. The model processes inputs and outputs cyclically in each time slice. The output channel generates new tokens autoregressively. The input channel prefills the key-value cache and predicts next tokens. Tokens in input and output channels do not attend to each other. A channel-aware causal mask is modified to accommodate token dependency. State token <1> signals that the input is a user query. Upon <1>, the original output channel is suspended. State token <2> denotes that the new input is no-query text. Upon <2>, the model continues to respond to the original query. DUO differs from MiniCPM-Duplex by not splitting and mixing time slices. DUO preserves the data format with only the addition of state tokens. The method is implemented using FlexAttention. DUO does not increase the number of forward passes compared to standard decoding. The key-value cache of the predicted tokens is managed for transitions.

Key Results
MiniCPM-Duo demonstrates superior responsiveness compared to MiniCPM-Duplex. MiniCPM-Duo demonstrates superior human-likeness compared to MiniCPM-Duplex. MiniCPM-Duo maintains comparable levels of factuality and faithfulness. MiniCPM-Duo exhibits a substantial advantage in overall performance. MiniCPM-Duo achieves comparable results with MiniCPM on standard benchmarks. MiniCPM-Duo achieves 50.66 on CMMLU compared to 50.56 for MiniCPM. MiniCPM-Duo achieves 53.13 on MMLU compared to 53.45 for MiniCPM. MiniCPM-Duo achieves 36.51 on BBH compared to 37.25 for MiniCPM. MiniCPM-Duo achieves 51.83 on HumanEval compared to 50.00 for MiniCPM. MiniCPM-Duo achieves 38.19 on MBPP compared to 38.09 for MiniCPM. MiniCPM-Duo achieves 42.15 on GSM8K compared to 42.30 for MiniCPM. MiniCPM-Duo achieves 84.93 on ARC-e compared to 84.60 for MiniCPM. MiniCPM-Duo achieves 70.48 on ARC-c compared to 69.80 for MiniCPM. MiniCPM-Duo achieves 59.78 on HellaSwag compared to 61.40 for MiniCPM. MiniCPM-Duplex performance drops when trained on the same 10K dataset scale. The duplex capability of inadequately trained MiniCPM-Duplex is relatively poor. Training DUO took 25 minutes versus 36 hours for MiniCPM-Duplex. Training DUO used 8 GPUs versus 40 GPUs for MiniCPM-Duplex.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
DUO equips models with duplex abilities requiring minimal training costs. The channel-division approach preserves the original model's capabilities. DUO enables real-time interactive feedback including non-awakening interactions. The method allows the model to handle user interruptions effectively. DUO functions as a versatile system adaptable to multimodal settings. Input tokens could be features extracted by encoders from various modalities. The approach broadens the potential applications of this technology.

Contradictions And Limitations
A significant constraint lies in the scope of multimodal testing. The experiments primarily focused on language models. This focus potentially limits the generalizability of findings to other domains. Future research aims to extend DUO to multimodal settings. The study has limitations regarding the scope of testing.

Claims
DUO achieves superior human-likeness and responsiveness with minimal training overhead. MiniCPM-Duo demonstrates superior responsiveness and human-likeness. MiniCPM-Duo exhibits a substantial advantage in overall performance. Training DUO took 25 minutes versus 36 hours for MiniCPM-Duplex. MiniCPM-Duo achieves 59.78 on HellaSwag compared to 61.40 for MiniCPM. The method offers a resource-efficient path toward real-time conversational AI.
DUO preserves original model capabilities better than time-division baselines on standard benchmarks. MiniCPM-Duo achieves comparable results with MiniCPM on standard benchmarks. MiniCPM-Duo preserves the model's original capabilities to a greater extent. MiniCPM-Duo achieves 59.78 on HellaSwag compared to 61.40 for MiniCPM. 

Data And Code Availability
The decoding strategy is implemented based on the repository 1. The interactive demo was originally developed for MiniCPM-Duplex.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The study studied how MiniCPM-Duplex performs when trained on the same scale dataset. The results show that performances drop when trained on smaller datasets. The duplex capability of inadequately trained MiniCPM-Duplex is relatively poor.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 illustrates the channel-based parallel decoding and channel transition. Figure 2 presents the comparison result between MiniCPM-Duo and MiniCPM-Duplex. Figure 3 shows a case study of user query and interruption handling. Table 1 presents the performances on standard benchmarks.

Three Takeaways
1. DUO enables duplex capabilities with minimal training costs. 2. The strongest evidence is the superior human-likeness and responsiveness. 3. The future path involves extending DUO to multimodal settings.
